item.title: Student Rep’s Corner: Allison Bryant
item.description: Hello ASP! My name is Allison Bryant, and I am the new student representative to the ASP Council for the 2024–2025 academic year. I am a PhD student working with Dr. Matthew Bolek at Oklahoma State University in Stillwater, OK. I study taxonomy, lifecycles, and life history of coccidia in lizards. I have been a student member and have attended ASP since 2021, where my first meeting was virtual! item.title: Crossing Continents: Insights on parasitology with Dr. Shokoofeh Shamsi
item.description: By: Hayden Krause Dr. Shokoofeh Shamsi is a professor of Veterinary Parasitology at Charles Sturt University in Wagga Wagga, Australia, known for her work in understanding the roles parasites have in ecosystems, discovering new species and connecting the gap between parasitology and public health. Her passion for parasitology began during her time as a student in her home country of Iran. item.title: Author’s Corner: Dr. Chelsea Wood
item.description: “Learning about the secret world of parasites turned my life upside down, leading me along a path that I would never have imagined for myself when I was sitting in my seventh-grade classroom. But among the most surprising twists in the tale of my scientific life is this one: I never thought that slimy, squirmy, poop-flecked parasites would lead me to – of all things – love.” -Chelsea Wood, Power to the Parasites! item.title: When Science Meets Art: Understanding Parasites Through Creative Expression
item.description: Interview by Hayden Krause Dr. Jerri Bartholomew is a retired professor of microbiology at Oregon State University and a previous member on the ASP awards committee. Jerri remains in touch with her research through her continued role as the Director of the J. L. Fryer Aquatic Animal Health Laboratory and expression of her scientific findings using art. item.title: Call for Bernie Fried Student Research Grant proposals
item.description: The American Society of Parasitologists is pleased to announce the inaugural call for proposals for the Bernie Fried Student Research Grant. Information and application instructions can be found here. The application deadline is January 15, 2026. Questions about the process may be directed to the chair of the Bernie Fried Grants Awards Committee, Dr. Joanna Cielocha (Joanna.Cielocha@rockhurst.edu).
